To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the explicit consideration of the background score distributions of each subject in profile comparison improves remote protein sequence homology detection, and that this improvement is particularly significant when these distributions are constructed from the complete set of non-homology database representatives for the subject.

(i) explicit consideration of background distribution of scores for the database templates (subjects) improves the quality of homologous sequence profile comparison; (ii) the increase in performance due to the use of background distributions is larger when the distributions are calculated using all known non-homers rather than a small subset of database representatives; and that (iii) the all known non-homer distributions make the dominant contribution: adding the calibration subset distribution has a negligible additional impact on performance.

(1) inclusion of background score distributions in profile-based sequence comparison increases the sensitivity of homology detection, and (2) this increase is more pronounced when these distributions are constructed based on all known non-homers of a subject rather than on a small calibration subset.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of more effective and efficient methods for protein sequence analysis and the inference of protein structure, evolution and function.
the development of a novel approach to improve the accuracy of remote homology detection by explicitly considering background score distributions for the database templates.
a new method for the statistical evaluation of remote homology detection and shows that it is possible to achieve better results by explicitly considering scores between unrelated proteins.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the consideration of the background score distributions of the database templates (subject) in profile comparisons improves the performance of homology detection.

the inclusion of background distributions of scores for each subject in the calculation of the statistical significance of detected similarity between a query and a subject is a powerful method to increase the accuracy of profile comparison.
the consideration of the complete set of non-homology scores for each subject is the best way to improve the statistical significance of detected homology.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have shown the importance of the subject-based score distribution in the estimation of the statistical significance of the profile similarity.
the consideration of scores between unrelated proteins improves profile comparison.
the explicit consideration of the background distributions of scores to all known database proteins for each subject improves the performance of profile comparison.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the consideration of the background score distributions for the subjects in the database improves the quality of remote homology detection.
the consideration of the background score distributions for all known non-homers for each database template improves the performance of profile-based comparison.
, when the subject database is known to contain non-homologous proteins, one should explicitly account for this fact in estimating the statistical significance of detected similarities.
